display_name: Nominal Price Illusion x Momentum Factor
summary_html:
Nominal Price Illusion x Momentum Factor

策略概述

This paper documents that the stock momentum effect is significantly stronger among assets with high nominal price illusion -- i.e., assets whose prices are low relative to fundamentals. The mechanism is behavioral: investors overestimate the upside potential of low-priced assets, causing loser stocks with low nominal prices to be overvalued and subsequently underperform, amplifying momentum profits.

For commodities, we adapt the paper's log PRC* measure (originally the fitted value from a cross-sectional regression of stock price on book value, earnings, total assets, and dividends) using the negative log of the commodity futures closing price as a proxy for nominal price illusion. This captures the same behavioral channel: low-priced commodities may attract speculative optimism. The key tradeable factor is the interaction between momentum rank and price-illusion rank: buy commodities with both high momentum and high illusion (low price), short those with low momentum and low illusion (high price).

数学公式

Momentum (MOM):

\text{MOM}_{i,t} = \frac{P_{i,t-21}}{P_{i,t-273}} - 1

11-month cumulative return, skipping the most recent month (21 trading days).

Nominal Price Illusion Proxy:

\text{NPI}_{i,t} = -\ln(P_{i,t})

Negative log price -- higher values indicate greater illusion (lower absolute price).

Price-Momentum Interaction:

\text{Signal}_{i,t} = \text{rank}_{\text{CS}}(\text{MOM}_{i,t}) \times \text{rank}_{\text{CS}}(\text{NPI}_{i,t})

Cross-sectional rank product of momentum and price illusion.

Position:

\text{pos}_{i,t} = \frac{(\text{rank}(\text{Signal}) - 0.5) \times 2 \times \sigma_{\text{target}}}{\hat{\sigma}_{i,t} \times \sqrt{252}}

Vol-target scaled continuous long-short position.

改进历程

R1 (Sharpe 0.81): Initial implementation with all four factors from the paper -- pure momentum, price illusion (neg log price), MAX (max daily return), and realized skewness -- plus their pairwise and triple interactions with momentum. 10 variants covering 3 momentum windows (63d, 126d, 252d) and all factor combinations. The price-momentum interaction at 252d immediately stood out as the best factor (0.81), validating the paper's core finding. Key diagnostic: TS IC was only 0.005 with 54% positive symbols, suggesting room for filtering or parameter tuning.

R2 (Sharpe 0.94): Diagnosed that the monthly rebalance (hold=21d) was suboptimal -- the momentum signal updates daily but positions only refresh monthly. Shortened hold period to 10 days, which reduced signal lag and improved Sharpe to 0.94 (+16%). Also tested IC-gating (filtering weak symbols) and hold=42d; IC-gating showed no improvement (same Sharpe as ungated), confirming the signal is broadly effective across symbols. The hold=10d variant was the clear winner -- the key turning point of the iteration.

R3 (Sharpe 0.90): Fine-tuned hold period grid (5d, 10d, 15d, 21d) and vol-target (0.10, 0.15, 0.20). Also created a weighted combo of price-momentum and triple interaction. Hold=15d scored 0.90, hold=5d was similar but noisier. Vol-target variations did not improve over 0.15. The combo variant (0.83) was decent but didn't beat the pure price-momentum interaction. Pipeline auto-restored to R2's spec_best (0.94).
